title: The Broken Garden
premise: Yara Ravensworth, a cartographer of unmapped realms hiding his magic in a city that outlawed it, discovers the old gods are answering prayers again — and that one of those prayers was made by his late mother, who sold Yara's soul to the court beneath the mountain to save him as a child. To reclaim it, he must map a road through the unmapped Undercourt, allying with Sef, a disgraced temple knight sworn to destroy what Yara is. As love blooms between them against duty's iron law, Yara learns he is not merely a charm-seller but the last heir of the Raven Throne, and the gods' return is his inheritance calling him home. In the end, Yara trades his reclaimed soul for the freedom of every soul in the Undercourt, becoming a living map between worlds — and chooses Sef, and the broken garden of his childhood, over the throne.
about_author: Rafael Sandoval is a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to maps of places that do not exist. He writes in a converted lighthouse on the northern coast, where he keeps an herbarium of plants that have never bloomed.

chapters.title: The City That Forbade Wonder
chapters.summary: Yara sells a luck-charm to a desperate widow in Grayharbor's night market, concealing the true magic beneath the trinket. His POV establishes his double life: cartographer by day, outlaw by night. The emotional beat is weary vigilance — he has survived three years by being small.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: A candle Yara charmed burns blue instead of gold, and the widow's dying son wakes healed. Old magic, dead for a century, is moving. Yara feels it like a hook behind his ribs. The beat is dread mixed with a terrible homesickness for something he cannot name.

chapters.title: The Knight at the Door
chapters.summary: Sef Andric, a temple knight stripped of rank for heresy, arrives investigating answered prayers and nearly catches Yara mid-rite. Their first clash is verbal, electric, mutual recognition of something forbidden. The beat is wary attraction sharpened by danger.

chapters.title: Maps of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Yara's hidden workshop is revealed: charts of realms no living person has seen, drawn in his mother's hand and his own. Sef finds them and realizes the outlaw she hunts may be the only guide into whatever is waking below. Beat: reluctant alliance forged over ink and secrets.

chapters.title: What Mother Sold
chapters.summary: Among the maps Yara finds a contract bearing his own name — his mother sold his soul to the Undercourt the night he was born. The gods' return has activated the debt; collectors will come within a season. Beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The First Collector
chapters.summary: A pale figure of folded shadow appears in Grayharbor, tasting the air for Yara's name. He escapes through a door he paints onto a wall with blood and chalk. Beat: terror, and the first proof his cartography is itself a kind of magic.

chapters.title: Oathbreaking
chapters.summary: Sef must choose: report Yara to the temple and end this, or go rogue and follow him down. She burns her warrant. Beat: duty breaking cleanly, like ice underfoot, and the strange lightness after.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath the World
chapters.summary: They descend through a collapsed mine Yara once mapped from dreams, following a river that flows uphill. The world thins; memories leak out of the stone. Beat: intimacy born of shared darkness and shared fear.

chapters.title: The Garden That Was
chapters.summary: They pass the ruin of Ravensworth, Yara's ancestral estate, its gardens petrified mid-bloom. He remembers nothing of it, yet his feet know every path. Beat: identity trembling loose from its moorings.

chapters.title: The God of Small Doors
chapters.summary: A minor god, trapped in a mousehole since the outlawry, bargains passage for a promise: Yara will open all doors when he comes into power. Neither understands the promise's weight yet. Beat: wonder rekindled, priced in ignorance.

chapters.title: Toll
chapters.summary: The river demands payment in memory. Sef gives up her sister's face; Yara secretly pays double so she keeps something. Beat: love expressed as theft, tender and dishonest.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: They reach the Undercourt: a cathedral of roots where sold souls hang like lanterns, each burning with the life its owner never lived. Yara finds his own lantern, dim but unlit. Beat: awe curdled into horror.

chapters.title: The Regent of Roots
chapters.summary: The Undercourt's regent, wearing Yara's mother's borrowed face, explains the terms: the soul can be bought back only with something of equal weight. Beat: negotiation as seduction; the regent wants Yara for reasons beyond contract.

chapters.title: Why She Did It
chapters.summary: In the regent's archive, Sef reads the original bargain: Yara's mother traded his soul to hide him from the Raven Throne's assassins. The sale was protection. Beat: fury at his mother dissolving into heartbreak.

chapters.title: Equal Weight
chapters.summary: The regent names the price: a crown, a god, or a willing soul freely given. They retreat to plan, and Yara quietly decides which he can spare. Beat: self-erasure disguised as strategy.

chapters.title: The Temple's Hounds
chapters.summary: Temple inquisitors, tracking Sef, breach the upper ways. The two flee deeper, and Sef kills for the first time since her fall. Beat: guilt and Yara's unexpected gentleness with her afterward.

chapters.title: Lantern-Light Confessions
chapters.summary: Among the hanging souls, they speak their truths: her heresy was believing the gods should be free; his crime was existing. First kiss, witnessed by a thousand borrowed lights. Beat: love declared in the worst possible place.

chapters.title: The Raven Throne
chapters.summary: Yara's blood opens a sealed vault in the Undercourt's depths, revealing the truth of his inheritance: he is heir to the Raven Throne, and the old gods went silent because his family bound them. Beat: identity detonated — he is not the victim of the old order but its last pillar.

chapters.title: What the Gods Were For
chapters.summary: A chained god, half-mad, tells Sef how the Ravensworth line fed on worship, and why the outlawry was righteous. Her love and her faith collide. Beat: the romance's central fracture.

chapters.title: Departure Without Goodbye
chapters.summary: Sef leaves the Undercourt alone, unable to help the man she loves unmake the world she swore to heal. Yara lets her go, believing he deserves it. Beat: heartbreak as moral choice, both sides right.

chapters.title: The Bargain Struck
chapters.summary: Alone, Yara offers the regent his freely given soul in exchange for his own lantern — trading a future for a past. The regent accepts, delighted: a Raven soul will feed the court for centuries. Beat: sacrifice signed in good faith and bad information.

chapters.title: Ascension
chapters.summary: Back on the surface, Yara's claim activates: the bound gods wake fully and kneel to him. Grayharbor's outlawed magic erupts everywhere at once. He is suddenly the most powerful and most hunted person alive. Beat: triumph that feels like drowning.

chapters.title: The Broken Garden Blooms
chapters.summary: Ravensworth's petrified garden flowers overnight, drawing pilgrims, inquisitors, and assassins. Yara returns to his inheritance and hates every stone of it. Beat: homecoming as estrangement.

chapters.title: The Temple's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: The high temple offers Sef full restoration if she kills the last Raven. She asks for three days. Beat: duty rebuilt on the ruins of love, aimed at the person she loves.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Sef comes to Ravensworth not as assassin but as warning: the temple marches, and worse things march behind it. They spend the days together as if time were already spent. Beat: stolen happiness with a blade in its pocket.

chapters.title: The Regent's Gambit
chapters.summary: The regent surfaces wearing Yara's mother's face, offering the city peace in exchange for the heir. The crowd wavers; the widow from chapter one speaks for him. Beat: public judgment, private gratitude repaid.

chapters.title: Doors Opening
chapters.summary: Yara honors the mouse-god's bargain, unlocking every seal his ancestors set — including the ones binding the gods' hunger. Freed, some gods choose mercy; others do not. Beat: a promise kept that breaks the world open.

chapters.title: Night of the Unbound
chapters.summary: Unbound gods war above Grayharbor. Sef defends civilians alongside temple knights who still mean to kill Yara. Beat: chaos as crucible; her two loyalties forced into a single body.

chapters.title: The Price Comes Due
chapters.summary: The regent collects Yara's promised soul early, and he begins to fade — footprints vanishing behind him, his name slipping from minds. Only Sef, loving him against her oaths, remembers. Beat: erasure as the ultimate stake; love as the only anchor.

chapters.title: The Map of One Person
chapters.summary: Sef carries Yara toward the Undercourt, navigating by memory of him alone, while he forgets himself chapter by chapter. She narrates their story back to him to keep him real. Beat: the novel's emotional summit — identity held by another's love.

chapters.title: Descent of the Remembering
chapters.summary: They breach the Undercourt as Yara forgets her face. The regent greets them, certain of victory. Beat: calm before the climax, everything staked.

chapters.title: The Court Revolt
chapters.summary: The hanging souls, stirred by Yara's fading light, rise against the regent — every stolen life wanting its weight back. The cathedral of roots burns cold. Beat: uprising as catharsis.

chapters.title: Mother's Face
chapters.summary: Yara confronts the regent wearing his mother's face and finally grieves her properly — then rejects the mask. Grief completes, power clarifies. Beat: the personal wound closed so the final fight can be fought clean.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Soul
chapters.summary: Climax: Yara refuses both options — no throne, no sacrifice. Instead he does what he was always meant to do: he maps. He draws the Undercourt into the world's atlas, making it known, and what is truly known cannot hold souls captive. Beat: victory through his true nature, not his bloodline.

chapters.title: Lanterns Released
chapters.summary: The souls go free, streaming upward like reversed rain. The regent, unmasked as the first Raven ancestor who refused to die, dissolves when named. Beat: release, vast and quiet.

chapters.title: The Empty Throne
chapters.summary: The gods offer Yara the Raven Throne remade. He declines, and offers them something harder: accountability, worship freely given or not at all. Some accept; some walk away. Beat: power renounced on principled terms.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Sef returns to a temple transformed by the night of unbound gods; she is offered leadership and instead founds an order of door-openers. Beat: duty redefined rather than abandoned.

chapters.title: The Gardener
chapters.summary: Yara, mortal and unnamed by choice, replants Ravensworth's garden with seeds from every realm he mapped. The widow's son brings the first water. Beat: healing as slow work, chosen over glory.

chapters.title: Two Names on a Door
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Sef arrives at Ravensworth with no warrant and no orders, only herself. Yara carves both their names beside the garden gate. The old gods answer one last prayer — theirs — with simple sunlight. Beat: love chosen over duty fulfilled, inheritance rewritten as a garden kept.
